paper.title: Non-stochastic Best Arm Identification and Hyperparameter Optimization

unmapped: each arm's k-th pull yields loss l_{i,k} in R from a deterministic oblivious sequence that converges to a limit nu_i; the goal is to identify argmin_i nu_i
loss of an arm depends on its own pull count (rested), not on global time
performance characterized via unknown convergence envelopes gamma_i(t) with unknown rate
settings.definition_quote: Non-stochastic (proposed in this work) : For all $i \in [n]$, $k \geq 1$, let $\ell_{i,k} \in \R$ be generated by an oblivious adversary and assume $\nu_i = \lim_{\tau \rightarrow \infty} \ell_{i,\tau}$ exists. The goal is to identify $\arg\min_i \nu_i$ while minimizing $\sum_{i=1}^n T_i$.

symbols.M_SH: max_{i=2..n} i*(1 + gammabar^{-1}((nu_i - nu_1)/2)), arms sorted by limit nu_1 < nu_2 <= ... <= nu_n
symbols.gammabar: max_i gamma_i(t), the pointwise smallest non-increasing envelope with |l_{i,t} - nu_i| <= gamma_i(t)

conditions: limits nu_i exist; nu_1 < nu_2 (unique best arm)
tuning: budget B = T must exceed z

source.label: adaptive

results.notes: Sufficient budget (B=T, n=K) for deterministic identification of the best arm; recorded as sample complexity. Deterministic guarantee mapped to almost_sure.

symbols.gammainv_i: gammabar^{-1}((nu_i - nu_1)/2) = min{t : max_j gamma_j(t) <= (nu_i - nu_1)/2}

conditions: limits nu_i exist; nu_1 < nu_2 (unique best arm)
tuning: budget B = T must exceed this quantity

source.label: adaptive
source.quote: z \leq 2 \lceil \log_2(n) \rceil \big( n + \sum_{i=2,\dots,n} \bar{\gamma}^{-1} ( \tfrac{ \nu_i -\nu_1 }{2} ) \big). If the budget $B>z$ then the best arm is returned from the algorithm.

results.notes: Looser, interpretable form of the sufficient budget in Theorem 1.

symbols.G_max: max_{i>=2} gammabar^{-1}((nu_i - nu_1)/2), with gammabar = max_i gamma_i

conditions: B is a multiple of n

source.quote: For a budget $B$ and set of $n$ arms, define $\widehat{i}_{SH}$ as the output of the Successive Halving algorithm. Then \nu_{\widehat{i}_{SH}} - \nu_1 \leq \lceil\log_2(n)\rceil 2 \bar{\gamma}( \lfloor \tfrac{ B }{n \lceil \log_2(n) \rceil } \rfloor ).

results.notes: Simple regret in terms of limiting values nu; budget B mapped to T.
